text:
erin: Quick question 1 - I had my dependent get a meningitis booster while visiting family in Morocco and paid cash. Can we submit for reimbursement and can I add them retro as a student dependent? They're 22 and full-time at uni.

harper (Benefits): Short answer: likely yes if they meet full-time student definition. For the cash-paid vaccine we need the itemized receipt, proof of payment (card statement or receipt with clinic stamp), and a medical record or EOB if available. For retro add: enrollment form + enrollment letter + ID.

mike: Also confirm the vaccine code if available (CPT/ICD). Some carriers need a procedure code for immunizations to process. If clinic doesn't provide a code, send the clinical note instead.

erin: The receipt only lists "vaccin" and amount in MAD. Clinic gave a stamped note with vaccine name and date.

harper (Benefits): Send original + an English translation. Certified translation preferred but a clear translated note + photo of clinic stamp often works for intake. Include currency conversion for the date of service. Email docs to benefits@redwood.com with subject "Retro Vaccine Reimb - Erin [lastname]".

benefits-bot: Automated: Dependent Enrollment Form -> https://intranet.redwood.com/forms/dependent-enroll. Typical carrier processing 4-8 weeks. Internal intake confirmation within 1-2 business days. For urgent medical needs mark subject "URGENT".

erin: Will I get a digital ID card immediately after you submit the enrollment? I might need it for a follow-up in a month.

harper (Benefits): Carrier issues digital ID after they confirm enrollment. For retro adds we can produce an internal confirmation letter (1 business day) you can show to clinics in the meantime. That letter does not guarantee payment but helps direct-billing attempts.

erin: Thanks 1 I'll send the receipt, clinic note, passport page and uni letter tonight.

harper (Benefits): Great 1 include the card transaction screenshot for the payment if you have it. That speeds reimbursement.
